newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat takes complaints against Israel to Davos.
newsitem.headline: Arafat takes complaints against Israel to Davos.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Saturday took complaints that Israel is not keeping up its side of peace deals with the PLO to the world economic forum at the Swiss ski resort of Davos, a Palestinian minister said.

"We have of course written statements which the president will take with him to Davos...and we will submit it to the sponsors and of course to the international community," Education Minister Hanan Ashrawi told reporters in Gaza.

"We have taken a very clear decision that we will continue the renovation of homes and that Israel has no business preventing the renovation of homes in Hebron and we will continue all the plans in order to implement agreements."
Israel on January 17 handed 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule after months of acrimonious negotiations that strained Middle East peace efforts.
Palestinian lawmakers on Wednesday rejected an Israeli military order prohibiting Palestinians from renovating Arab buildings near Jewish enclaves. The enclaves are under Israeli control.
Ashrawi spoke to reporters after the Palestinian Authority cabinet meeting late on Friday night.
The cabinet in a statement complained that a joint committee on releasing Palestinian prisoners had yet to meet.

It also said that Israel was delaying work on a Gaza sea port and implementation of a "safe passage" between Gaza and the West Bank through Israel, preventing operation of Gaza airport and holding up in its ports donations from abroad.

"The continuation of these measures could mean the end of the current chance to continue the peace process and push the region and its people again into the past of clashes and confrontations," the cabinet statement said.

Addenda to the Hebron accord call for the sides to deal with prisoners, the sea and air ports, and the safe passage -- all issues remaining from earlier interim agreements -- and to begin final peace talks within two months of the Hebron handover.
"We urged Israel to comply, to form its negotiating teams and to start negotiating immediately," Ashrawi said.
Arafat left Gaza for Davos early on Saturday. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, already in Davos, will meet Arafat and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak separately on Sunday at the resort.
